blocks.text: A definite integral adds up a quantity over an interval. For the graph of a function it gives the signed area between the curve and the horizontal axis: area below the axis counts as negative. The fundamental theorem of calculus links it to derivatives: if $F' = f$ and $f$ is continuous, then $\int_a^b f(t)\, dt = F(b) - F(a)$, and differentiating the area function $\int_a^x f(t)\, dt$ gives back $f(x)$.
